title: Supply Chain Provenance Tracking
business: Logistics companies managing complex, multi-tier supplier networks.
problem: Traditional relational databases struggle to perform recursive lookups across deep supply chain dependencies, leading to slow visibility into the origin of raw materials.
solution: SurrealDB uses a multi-model approach where supply chain entities are stored as records and their dependencies are defined as typed graph edges, allowing for single-query recursive traversal of the entire lineage.
steps: Define schema-full tables for Suppliers and Components to enforce data integrity.
Create records for each entity representing a specific manufacturer or part.
Establish graph edges between records using the RELATE statement to represent supply dependencies.
Execute a single SurrealQL query using arrow syntax to traverse the graph from a finished product to its raw material origins.
Utilize ACID transactions to ensure that updates to supplier status and component relationships commit atomically.
outcome: Real-time visibility into the complete provenance of any product, enabling rapid identification of upstream bottlenecks or quality issues.
limitation: Deep recursive graph traversals can become computationally expensive as the depth of the supply chain increases; developers should monitor query execution time and consider indexing frequently traversed paths.
